sections.label: The Mandukya
sections.name: Om and the four states of the Self
intro: The shortest of the principal Upanishads, twelve verses long, and to many the deepest. It reads the sacred syllable Om as a map of consciousness: its sounds a, u and m are waking, dreaming and deep sleep, and the silence after it is the Fourth (turiya), the Self beyond them all. The great teacher Gaudapada wrote his Karika on it, and Shankara commented on both. Translated by Robert Ernest Hume (1921).

verses.sa:
ओमित्येतदक्षरमिदँ सर्वं तस्योपव्याख्यानभूतं भवद् भविष्यदिति सर्वमोङ्कार एव ।
यच्चान्यत् त्रिकालातीतं तदप्योङ्कार एव ॥
verses.tr:
omityetadakṣaramidam̐ sarvaṃ tasyopavyākhyānabhūtaṃ bhavad bhaviṣyaditi sarvamoṅkāra eva
yaccānyat trikālātītaṃ tadapyoṅkāra eva
verses.en: Om!—This syllable is this whole world. Its further explanation is:—The past, the present, the future—everything is just the word Om. And whatever else that transcends threefold time—that, too, is just the word Om.
verses.head: The mystic symbolism of the word Om: identified with the fourfold Brahman

verses.sa: सर्वं ह्येतद् ब्रह्मायमात्मा ब्रह्म सोऽयमात्मा चतुष्पात् ॥
verses.tr: sarvaṃ hyetad brahmāyamātmā brahma so'yamātmā catuṣpāt
verses.en: For truly, everything here is Brahma; this self (atman) is Brahma. This same self has four fourths.

verses.sa: जागरितस्थानो बहिःप्रज्ञः सप्ताङ्ग एकोनविंशतिमुखः स्थूलभुग्वैश्वानरः प्रथमः पादः ॥
verses.tr: jāgaritasthāno bahiḥprajñaḥ saptāṅga ekonaviṃśatimukhaḥ sthūlabhugvaiśvānaraḥ prathamaḥ pādaḥ
verses.en: The waking state (jagarita-sthana), outwardly cognitive, having seven limbs, having nineteen mouths, enjoying the gross (sthula-bhuj), the Common-to-all-men (vaisvanara), is the first fourth.
verses.head: The word Om, in its sounds, as the four states of the Self

verses.sa: स्वप्नस्थानोऽन्तःप्रज्ञः सप्ताङ्ग एकोनविंशतिमुखः प्रविविक्तभुक्तैजसो द्वितीयः पादः ॥
verses.tr: svapnasthāno'ntaḥprajñaḥ saptāṅga ekonaviṃśatimukhaḥ praviviktabhuktaijaso dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ
verses.en: The dreaming state (svapna-sthana), inwardly cognitive, having seven limbs, having nineteen mouths, enjoying the exquisite (pravivikta-bhuj), the Brilliant (taijasa), is the second fourth.

verses.sa:
यत्र सुप्तो न कञ्चन कामं कामयते न कञ्चन स्वप्नं पश्यति तत् सुषुप्तम् ।
सुषुप्तस्थान एकीभूतः प्रज्ञानघन एवानन्दमयो ह्यानन्दभुक् चेतोमुखः प्राज्ञस्तृतीयः पादः ॥
verses.tr:
yatra supto na kañcana kāmaṃ kāmayate na kañcana svapnaṃ paśyati tat suṣuptam
suṣuptasthāna ekībhūtaḥ prajñānaghana evānandamayo hyānandabhuk cetomukhaḥ prājñastṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ
verses.en: If one asleep desires no desire whatsoever, sees no dream whatsoever, that is deep sleep (sushupta). The deep-sleep state (sushupta-sthana), unified (eki-bhuta), just (eva) a cognition-mass (prajnana-ghana), consisting of bliss (ananda-maya), enjoying bliss (ananda-bhuj), whose mouth is thought (cetas-), the Cognitional (prajna), is the third fourth.

verses.sa: एष सर्वेश्वर एष सर्वज्ञ एषोऽन्तर्याम्येष योनिः सर्वस्य प्रभवाप्ययौ हि भूतानाम् ॥
verses.tr: eṣa sarveśvara eṣa sarvajña eṣo'ntaryāmyeṣa yoniḥ sarvasya prabhavāpyayau hi bhūtānām
verses.en: This is the lord of all (sarvesvara). This is the all-knowing (sarva-jna). This is the inner controller (antaryamin). This is the source (yoni) of all, for this is the origin and the end (prabhavapyayau) of beings.

verses.sa:
नान्तःप्रज्ञं न बहिष्प्रज्ञं नोभयतःप्रज्ञं न प्रज्ञानघनं न प्रज्ञं नाप्रज्ञम् ।
अदृष्टमव्यवहार्यमग्राह्यमलक्षणं अचिन्त्यमव्यपदेश्यमेकात्मप्रत्ययासारं प्रपञ्चोपशमं शान्तं शिवमद्वैतं चतुर्थं मन्यन्ते स आत्मा स विज्ञेयः ॥
verses.tr:
nāntaḥprajñaṃ na bahiṣprajñaṃ nobhayataḥprajñaṃ na prajñānaghanaṃ na prajñaṃ nāprajñam
adṛṣṭamavyavahāryamagrāhyamalakṣaṇaṃ acintyamavyapadeśyamekātmapratyayāsāraṃ prapañcopaśamaṃ śāntaṃ śivamadvaitaṃ caturthaṃ manyante sa ātmā sa vijñeyaḥ
verses.en: Not inwardly cognitive (antah-prajna), not outwardly cognitive (bahih-prajna), not both-wise cognitive (ubhayatah-prajna), not a cognition-mass (prajnana-ghana), not cognitive (prajna), not non-cognitive (a-prajna), unseen (a-drishta), with which there can be no dealing (a-vyavaharya), ungraspable (a-grahya), having no distinctive mark (a-lakshana), non-thinkable (a-cintya), that cannot be designated (a-vyapadesya), the essence of the assurance of which is the state of being one with the Self (ekatmya-pratyaya-sara), the cessation of development (prapancopasama), tranquil (santa), benign (siva), without a second (a-dvaita)—[such] they think is the fourth. He is the Self (Atman). He should be discerned.

verses.sa: सोऽयमात्माऽध्यक्षरमोङ्कारोऽधिमात्रं पादा मात्रा मात्राश्च पादा अकार उकारो मकार इति ॥
verses.tr: so'yamātmā'dhyakṣaramoṅkāro'dhimātraṃ pādā mātrā mātrāśca pādā akāra ukāro makāra iti
verses.en: This is the Self with regard to the word Om, with regard to its elements. The elements (matra) are the fourths; the fourths, the elements: the letter a, the letter u, the letter m.

verses.sa: जागरितस्थानो वैश्वानरोऽकारः प्रथमा मात्राऽऽप्तेरादिमत्त्वाद्वाऽऽप्नोति ह वै सर्वान् कामानादिश्च भवति य एवं वेद ॥
verses.tr: jāgaritasthāno vaiśvānaro'kāraḥ prathamā mātrā''pterādimattvādvā''pnoti ha vai sarvān kāmānādiśca bhavati ya evaṃ veda
verses.en: The waking state, the Common-to-all-men, is the letter a, the first element, from apti ('obtaining') or from adimatva ('being first'). He obtains, verily, indeed, all desires, he becomes first—he who knows this.

verses.sa: स्वप्नस्थानस्तैजस उकारो द्वितीया मात्रोत्कर्षादुभयत्वाद्वोत्कर्षति ह वै ज्ञानसन्ततिं समानश्च भवति नास्याऽब्रह्मवित्कुले भवति य एवं वेद ॥
verses.tr: svapnasthānastaijasa ukāro dvitīyā mātrotkarṣādubhayatvādvotkarṣati ha vai jñānasantatiṃ samānaśca bhavati nāsyā'brahmavitkule bhavati ya evaṃ veda
verses.en: The sleeping state, the Brilliant, is the letter u, the second element, from utkarsha ('exaltation') or from ubhayatva ('intermediateness'). He exalts, verily, indeed, the continuity of knowledge; and he becomes equal (samana); no one ignorant of Brahma is born in the family of him who knows this.

verses.sa: सुषुप्तस्थानः प्राज्ञो मकारस्तृतीया मात्रा मितेरपीतेर्वा मिनोति ह वा इदं सर्वमपीतिश्च भवति य एवं वेद ॥
verses.tr: suṣuptasthānaḥ prājño makārastṛtīyā mātrā miterapītervā minoti ha vā idaṃ sarvamapītiśca bhavati ya evaṃ veda
verses.en: The deep-sleep state, the Cognitional, is the letter m, the third element, from miti ('erecting') or from apiti ('immerging'). He, verily, indeed, erects (minoti) this whole world, and he becomes its immerging—he who knows this.

verses.sa: अमात्रश्चतुर्थोऽव्यवहार्यः प्रपञ्चोपशमः शिवोऽद्वैत एवमोङ्कार आत्मैव संविशत्यात्मनाऽऽत्मानं य एवं वेद ॥
verses.tr: amātraścaturtho'vyavahāryaḥ prapañcopaśamaḥ śivo'dvaita evamoṅkāra ātmaiva saṃviśatyātmanā''tmānaṃ ya evaṃ veda
verses.en: The fourth is without an element, with which there can be no dealing, the cessation of development, benign, without a second. Thus Om is the Self (Atman) indeed. He who knows this, with his self enters the Self—yea, he who knows this!
